requirement:
For every non-distributed requirement's structural check under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, every direct implementation
reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source
selection to the initial mandatory inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, including when the requirement
also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. An in-source reference selects
its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline;
an anchor selects its named file or node. Source access, exclusions, errors,
and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. Refining
declarations continue to contribute their complete text. Implementation
helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively.
rationale:
**Verdict:** The tests adequately cover the requirement except for one known gap: the mixed test-and-implementation case. That gap is acknowledged by an open `{fixme}`.

**Obligations derived from `requirements.authoring.structural_inputs`, and the tests that cover them**

The two tests are `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[structural_roots_select_inputs_and_version_the_reference_digest]` and `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[structural_roots_obey_mandatory_access_and_resolution_rules]`.

- **In-source `{impl}` reference selects its enclosing node.**
  - The unanchored case asserts `unanchored.mandatory_inputs() == inputs`.
  - The input is `fn[api]` and its text contains `helper();`.
- **`:impl:` anchor selects its named node or file.**
  - The anchor `src/lib.rs#fn[api]` yields a single `fn[api]` input.
  - An anchor-only case, with no in-source reference, asserts `structural`.
  - The anchor `evidence/generated.rs` contributes that file.
- **Deduplication.** The anchor and the in-source reference select the same node, and the test asserts exactly one root.
- **Files without a language outline.** `src/details.txt` is supplied whole, with `item == ""` and the full text asserted.
- **Refining declarations contribute complete text.** The test asserts that both "Complete refinement." and "Second paragraph." appear for `requirements.refined`.
- **No recursive helper supply.** The root text is asserted not to contain `fn helper`.
- **Source access, exclusions and errors.**
  - A gitignored `src/lib.rs` makes `prepare` fail with an error containing "excluded".
  - An anchor to a missing node, `fn[missing]`, fails with an error containing "missing".
  - The `evidence/` path is allowed.
  - The test is also marked for `read_denial.mandatory`.
- **Non-distributed requirements only.** Examples, distributed requirements (a `sites` block) and requirements with no implementation edges are asserted not to be structural.
- **Refined requirement with no reaching root.** A requirement whose only implementation reference is on a refining declaration, and whose own text has none, is asserted not to be structural.
- **Dependency tracking.**
  - Changing the implementation makes a stored review stale with an "input … changed" error.
  - The reference-set digest changes with the structural inputs.

**Known gap, acknowledged.** The requirement says implementation roots MUST contribute "including when the requirement also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors".
- The mixed-case assertions in the first test contradict this: `!tested.structural`, and no `fn[api]` input appears. The same holds for the test-anchor variant.
- A `{fixme}` on `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare_with_context]` describes exactly this gap. It says implementation roots are mandatory only in exclusive structural mode and that the input tests assert the accepted compromise.
- It names `nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#51`, which is open.
- The gap is therefore acknowledged, and I found no other unacknowledged gaps.

text: :::{req} structural_inputs
For every non-distributed requirement's structural check under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, every direct implementation
reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source
selection to the initial mandatory inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, including when the requirement
also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. An in-source reference selects
its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline;
an anchor selects its named file or node. Source access, exclusions, errors,
and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. Refining
declarations continue to contribute their complete text. Implementation
helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively.
:::{req} structural_review
For every non-distributed requirement, the assessment MUST identify its stated
structural properties, including signatures, type and field relationships,
ownership, and required delegation through interfaces. With incoming `{impl}`
references or `:impl:` anchors, it MUST check that the supplied implementation
roots support every such property under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_prompt`. Without those edges, it MUST
establish that the requirement has no structural properties needing
implementation evidence; an unmet structural obligation MUST be a gap.
Incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors MUST NOT skip this check.
References and anchors are those considered under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery` and {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`. Obligations
delegated to refining declarations follow
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`. Examples, distributed requirements,
citation reviews, and site reviews retain their own assessment tasks.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
A file selected as a mandatory input MUST be visible under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`. A denied selection MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
